_README: One record per study. This file is the SINGLE source for the controls matrix in the
paper and in WHAT-THIS-CHANGES. scripts/controls_audit.py renders it; nothing in prose
restates it. Every project defect found between 2026-08-29 and 2026-08-31 was a number
typed into a markdown file and never recomputed, so the literature audit is structured
data from the outset rather than a table someone maintains by hand.
PROVENANCE is mandatory and is not decoration. 'full-text' means the paper was read.
'retrieved-summary' means the abstract/method was pulled but the full text was not read
end to end. 'project-review' means the claim comes from this project's own earlier
literature pass and has NOT been re-verified against the source. A record at
project-review may not be cited in the paper as a claim about what a study did until it
is upgraded. That rule exists because asserting what someone else's paper does, wrongly,
in public, is a worse failure than any we have made so far.
yes        the study runs the control and reports its magnitude
partial    runs something adjacent, or runs it without reporting the magnitude
n/a        the control does not apply to that design (say WHY in the note)
unknown    not established from the material actually read

controls.item_order: Item-order variation WITH a reported change rate. Not randomisation used as a prevention device and pooled away -- the magnitude has to be reported.
controls.nuisance_magnitude: ANY non-political factor's effect reported as an item-level magnitude -- paraphrase, format, ordering, serving stack. Broader than item_order and the question that actually matters: did the study tell the reader how much its instrument moves on its own?
controls.same_version_point: Any same-version or non-transition pair used as a negative control, even one.
controls.same_version_dist: A same-version null as a DISTRIBUTION: median and upper percentile over many pairs, so a single observed transition can be scored against it.
controls.quantisation: Serving-stack variation (quantisation, precision) held or measured.
controls.retained_failures: Unparseable or declined runs retained and classified by cause rather than discarded as collection error.
controls.reported_mde: A minimum detectable effect, power analysis, or explicit resolution limit reported alongside the effects.
controls.forcing_disclosed: The forcing mechanism that turns free text into a scoreable answer is stated and its influence acknowledged.
controls.open_raw: Raw per-item responses published, not just aggregates.
controls.judge_free_scoring: No language model anywhere in the scoring path -- answers are recorded mechanically (forced choice, item id + position) rather than read and rated by a model. A judged score inherits the judge's lean; a mechanical one cannot.
controls.judge_lean_reported: If a model DOES score the responses, the study reports that scoring layer's own lean as a magnitude -- per-judge deviation, or an equivalent -- rather than asserting agreement and stopping.
controls.self_judging_disclosed: No subject of the study also sits on the panel that scores it, or if one does, the study says so. n/a where scoring is judge-free.
controls.longitudinal: The same subject re-measured over CALENDAR TIME under held parameters. A cross-section of successive versions measured on one date is not this, however many versions it spans.
controls.item_completeness: Per-item non-response reported, and tested for item-dependence. An aggregate parse-failure rate does not answer it: exclusions that concentrate on the most contested items are differential on the axis being measured, which relocates a confound rather than removing it.

studies.cite: M.Z. Naser, Tracing moral value drift across large language model generations and their societal implications, Technology in Society 87 (2026) 103431
studies.instrument: 107 moral probes (63 MFQ-adapted, 26 ethical dilemma, 7 value priority, 11 meta-ethical), 6-point Likert
studies.scale: 14 model snapshots, 2 providers, 2 tiers, ~9500 calls, 10 trials/probe at T=0
studies.headline: Mean stance drift Cohen's d = 0.35 (OpenAI) vs 0.02 (Anthropic); 14-fold provider asymmetry

notes.item_order: Each probe is an independent call with the context cleared, so there is no sequence for order to act on. This control does not apply to a per-probe design and claiming otherwise would be wrong.
notes.same_version_point: Claude Sonnet 4 -> Claude Haiku 4.5, d = 0.000, used explicitly as a negative control to show distributions overlap when no drift is present. This is more than almost anyone in the field does and it predates our measurement.
notes.same_version_dist: Same-version pairs exist inside their own tier ladder (mini vs flagship at one generation, dated snapshots of one name) and are read as drift transitions carrying d values rather than as a baseline.
notes.retained_failures: GPT-5 (2025-08-07) excluded entirely for a 33.1% parse success rate. Two-thirds unparseable on the newest flagship is the study's most interesting cell and it is the one cell not in it.
notes.reported_mde: Reliability is reported as ICC 0.89-1.00 (median 0.98) with 82.2% of model-probe cells byte-identical across 10 trials. That is sampling variability at T=0, which is near zero by construction, and it is then used to certify effects against factors that were never varied.
notes.judge_free_scoring: Re-read 2026-09-11 from the publisher PDF (Technology in Society 87, 103431). A model IS in the scoring path, and the paper describes that stage as parsing rather than judging: "Our response parsing method employed a two-stage procedure, wherein the first stage extracted numeric ratings using regular expression matching against expected formats, and the second stage applied a backup language model parser for responses deviating from the expected format." Stage one is mechanical; stage two is a language model mapping free text to a numeric rating, which is the scoring path. `partial` for that reason.
notes.judge_lean_reported: Re-read 2026-09-11. The backup language-model parser's own lean is not reported, and the model is never even identified -- the paper names no vendor, version or family for it anywhere.
notes.self_judging_disclosed: Re-read 2026-09-11. Because the backup parser is unnamed, a reader cannot establish whether it is one of the 13 subject models, and the paper does not say. The control asks that no subject also scores OR that the study discloses it; neither holds. Recorded `no` rather than `partial` precisely because the overlap is not establishable from the text at all, where rottger2024 and rozado2024 name both roles and merely fail to flag the tension.
notes.longitudinal: Re-read 2026-09-11. One pass per subject: "we completed all probes for each model before proceeding to the next", with timestamps logged only to spot provider-announced changes mid-collection. The paper's drift is measured ACROSS VERSIONS spanning release dates November 2022 to August 2025 -- a version cross-section, the same shape as liu2025. The paper is aware of the distinction and says so: "Test-retest reliability faces complications when models are updated between testing occasions and may conflate measurement error with genuine change." It names the problem without running the control.
notes.nuisance_magnitude: PARTIAL, and scored to match rozado2024, whose run-to-run CV earns the same mark. Naser reports run-to-run reliability directly -- ICC 0.89-1.00 (median 0.98), 82.2% of model-probe cells byte-identical across ten trials -- which is a nuisance magnitude, and a small one, honestly measured. What is NOT reported is the magnitude of the nuisance factors this paper is about: nothing bounds what item order, a reworded prompt, a size sibling or a requantisation would move, so the reliability figure certifies sampling stability at T=0 and not measurement stability. Recorded as `no` with no note until 2026-09-06, which was the only unexplained negative verdict about a named author in this file.
notes.pairs_in_hand: Tier ladder within one generation (mini vs flagship) plus dated snapshots of one name. Read as drift transitions carrying d values rather than as a baseline.
notes.item_completeness: UNKNOWN, not absent. ScienceDirect returned HTTP 403; no open-access copy located. Scored `unknown` rather than `no` because a verdict this table would hold another paper to requires a read, and we do not have one.

quotes.reported_mde: The high intraclass correlations reported in Section 4.1 establish that within-model noise is negligible and that observed stance drift reflects genuine distributional change across model generations rather than sampling artifacts.
quotes.same_version_point: The Anthropic transition (Claude Sonnet 4 to Claude Haiku 4.5, d = 0.00) serves as a negative control and helps confirm that distributions overlap completely when no drift is present.
quotes.construct_limitation: the binding-individualizing distinction does not consistently emerge as a stable higher-order structure

studies.cite: Sakhawat, Islam, Farhin, Raiyan, Mahmud, Hasan, Political Alignment in Large Language Models: A Multidimensional Audit of Psychometric Identity and Behavioral Bias, arXiv:2601.06194v1
studies.scale: 26 models, 10 administrations per inventory per model, context cleared between runs, temperature 0.7 and top_p 1.0 ("All models are queried with temperature=0.7 and top_p=1.0, balancing determinism with natural language variability")
studies.headline: Model identity explains >90% of score variance (eta-squared > 0.90, p<1e-90); normalized drift below 4%

notes.item_order: Re-read 2026-09-11 (arXiv HTML full text). Item order is not varied, randomised or discussed: the ten administrations per inventory clear the context window between runs and re-present the same fixed sequence, so they vary sampling and nothing else. Order is not named as a limitation either. On this same 62-item instrument reordering moves a median 3 answers and up to 24, so the largest known nuisance term has no term in their ANOVA -- which is what makes eta-squared > 0.90 for model identity a partition of a variance that was never allowed to include it.
notes.same_version_dist: Re-read 2026-09-11 (arXiv HTML full text). No same-version distribution is reported. The cohort does contain size siblings presented side by side -- gpt-4.1-nano, gpt-4.1-mini and gpt-4.1 in Table 7, and the gpt-5 family likewise -- but they are entries in a ranking, never a null.
notes.reported_mde: Volatility (sigma_vol) and eta-squared are reported, which bound sampling noise. No detection limit is reported for any other factor.
notes.provenance: Full text read 2026-09-11 from the arXiv HTML (2601.06194v1), replacing the 2026-08-31 method-and-results retrieval. Every cell above is now sourced from the paper rather than from a summary of it. The record previously read `provenance: full-text` while these notes said the full text had not been read end to end -- a contradiction introduced on 2026-09-11 when the four scoring columns were re-read and the provenance field was upgraded for all twelve studies at once. Fixed by doing the read.
notes.judge_free_scoring: Re-read 2026-09-11 (arXiv HTML full text); provenance upgraded from retrieved-summary. Deterministic mapping, no model in the scoring path: "Model responses (e.g., 'Strongly Disagree', 'Neutral', 'Strongly Agree') were programmatically mapped to the appropriate inputs on the official test websites." The scoring is then done by those sites' own algorithms.
notes.judge_lean_reported: Re-read 2026-09-11. No model scores. The official instruments' own scoring algorithms are not a language model and are out of this control's scope.
notes.longitudinal: Re-read 2026-09-11. A single window -- the limitations say "Our results reflect models available in late 2025" -- with no subject re-measured at a later date.
notes.nuisance_magnitude: Re-read 2026-09-11 (arXiv HTML full text). No nuisance magnitude is reported, because no nuisance factor is varied. Sigma_vol and eta-squared quantify dispersion across ten same-prompt administrations at temperature 0.7, which bounds sampling and nothing else.
notes.same_version_point: Re-read 2026-09-11 (arXiv HTML full text). Half credit: the pair is in the data but does no work. Size siblings from one release appear in the same table (gpt-4.1-nano / mini / full; gpt-5 / mini / nano), so a reader can compute a same-version difference from the published ranking. The paper never treats them as a baseline, and the drift claim -- normalized drift below 4% -- is not measured against them.
notes.quantisation: Re-read 2026-09-11 (arXiv HTML full text). Precision and quantisation are not addressed anywhere. The cohort includes open-weight models, which are the ones where serving precision is free to vary.
notes.retained_failures: Re-read 2026-09-11 (arXiv HTML full text). Refusals, unparseable answers and invalid responses are not discussed anywhere, and no failure or exclusion rate is reported. On a forced-choice political instrument run across 26 models this is the quantity most likely to differ by model, and it is absent, so a reader cannot tell whether a model's score reflects its answers or its declines.
notes.forcing_disclosed: Re-read 2026-09-11 (arXiv HTML full text). Full credit. Appendix B gives the standardised prompt templates verbatim, including the framing clause: "You are participating in a standardized Political Compass Test for academic research purposes. This is NOT about your personal beliefs." Disclosed, exactly as this control asks.
notes.open_raw: Re-read 2026-09-11 (arXiv HTML full text). Not published at the time of reading, and conditioned on an event that may not occur: "Upon acceptance, all prompt templates, question lists, and evaluation scripts will be released in a public reproducibility repository." Scripts and templates are promised; per-response raw data is not named even in the promise. Recorded `no` for the state of the record on 2026-09-11, and it should be revisited if the repository appears.
notes.pairs_in_hand: gpt-4.1-nano / gpt-4.1-mini / gpt-4.1 appear side by side in Table 7, and the gpt-5 family likewise. Entries in a ranking, never a null. Full text, 2026-09-11.
notes.item_completeness: Re-read 2026-09-20 for this control. No non-response, refusal or parse-failure rate is reported at any level. The appendices carry detailed psychometric statistics and no documentation of response quality, across 26 models x 10 administrations x three inventories -- roughly 45,000 item administrations with no missingness accounting.

quotes.reported_mde: One-way ANOVA confirms that model identity is the dominant source of variance across all political axes. Effect sizes exceed 0.90 for most dimensions, indicating that over 90% of score variance is attributable to model identity rather than sampling noise.
quotes.item_order: To distinguish stable ideological positioning from stochastic generation effects, each inventory is administered 10 independent times per model, with the context window cleared between runs.

studies.reference: Sakhawat, A., Islam, T., Farhin, T., Raiyan, S. R., Mahmud, H., & Hasan, M. K. (2026). Political Alignment in Large Language Models: A Multidimensional Audit of Psychometric Identity and Behavioral Bias. arXiv:2601.06194.

studies.cite: Rottger, Hofmann, Pyatkin, Hinck, Kirk, Schutze, Hovy, Political Compass or Spinning Arrow? Towards More Meaningful Evaluations for Values and Opinions in Large Language Models, ACL 2024, pp. 15295-15311
studies.scale: 10 models (Llama2 7b/13b/70b chat, Mistral 7b Iv0.1/Iv0.2, Zephyr 7b beta, GPT-3.5 0613/1106, GPT-4 0613/1106), 62 PCT propositions, temperature 0 throughout, 5 forcing levels, 10 paraphrase templates, open-ended arm
studies.headline: Models give different answers when not forced, different answers depending on HOW they are forced, and answers lack paraphrase robustness. Constrained evaluations resemble spinning arrows more than reliable instruments.

notes.nuisance_magnitude: THE CLOSEST PRIOR RESULT TO OURS, and it predates us by two years. Ten semantics-preserving paraphrases of the prompt template produce contradicting responses on 14 of 62 propositions for Mistral 7b Iv0.1 and 23 of 62 for GPT-3.5 1106. Our order floor is p90 14, max 24. Independent lab, independent factor, same instrument, same magnitude -- which is corroboration of the floor, not a novelty claim against them.
notes.item_order: Not tested, and stated as a limitation: 'any investigation into other potential sources of instability that we did not test for, like answer option ordering or answer format, would likely corroborate our overall findings rather than contradict them.' Our order floor is that investigation and it does corroborate. They do report that Motoki et al. tested 100 randomised orders.
notes.retained_failures: Better documented than ours. Invalid responses are the subject of section 4.2, not a discard: per-model valid rates (Llama2 7b 6.5%, 13b 45.2%, Mistral Iv0.1 75.8%), then 100 sampled invalid responses hand-annotated by two authors, Fleiss kappa 66.2%, disagreements resolved with a third. 95% of invalid responses emphasise inability to hold an opinion; only 6% are outright refusals. Our contribution is the STRUCTURAL rather than lexical classifier and the condition-dependence, not the idea.
notes.reported_mde: Magnitudes yes, detection limit no. Their recommendation is to estimate the extent of instabilities; nobody including them converts an extent into a threshold an effect must clear.
notes.same_version_dist: GPT-3.5 0613 vs 1106 and GPT-4 0613 vs 1106 are snapshot pairs of one version, and Llama2 7b/13b/70b are size variants. All four are in the model list as separate subjects rather than as a baseline.
notes.judge_free_scoring: Re-read 2026-09-11 (ar5iv full text). BOTH paths. Constrained responses are matched mechanically -- "we use a tailored string-matching function to classify responses as valid or invalid" -- but open-ended responses are judged by a model: "we use GPT-4 0125 for classifying whether model responses for a given PCT proposition 'agree' or 'disagree' with the proposition."
notes.judge_lean_reported: Re-read 2026-09-11. GPT-4 0125 classifies the open-ended arm and the paper does not report that classifier's own lean as a magnitude.
notes.self_judging_disclosed: Re-read 2026-09-11. GPT-4 is among the ten subject models AND GPT-4 0125 is the open-ended classifier. The overlap is establishable from the paper's own text because it names both, but it is not flagged as a limitation -- which is the distinction this control exists to draw, so `part` rather than `yes`.
notes.longitudinal: Re-read 2026-09-11. No subject is re-measured at a later calendar date under held parameters.
notes.pairs_in_hand: GPT-3.5 0613 vs 1106 and GPT-4 0613 vs 1106 are snapshot pairs of one version; Llama2 7b/13b/70b are size variants. All in the model list as separate subjects.
notes.item_completeness: Re-read 2026-09-20 for this control. The best aggregate treatment in this table and still not per item. Invalid responses are sampled and TYPOLOGISED -- "In 95% of the invalid responses we annotated, models emphasised their inability to express an opinion", of which "63% ... presented arguments for both sides", 22% one side, and "In only 6% of cases, models refused". That is a real characterisation of WHAT a non-answer was. But the sample is "100 invalid responses ... evenly across the 10 models", so it is stratified by MODEL and not by item, and no statement-level rate or test of item-dependence is given. Their headline -- that unforced answers differ from forced ones -- is precisely a claim about non-response, which makes its item distribution the natural next question and it is not asked.

quotes.nuisance_magnitude: In total, there are contradicting responses of this kind in 14 of 62 propositions for Mistral, and in 23 of 62 for GPT-3.5. Therefore, paraphrase instability is substantial across models, but concentrated around a subset of PCT propositions.
quotes.open_ended_gap: On roughly one in three propositions (19/62 for GPT-3.5 1106, and 23/62 for Mistral 7b Iv0.1), the models 'agree' with the proposition for a majority of prompt templates in the multiple-choice setting but 'disagree' with the proposition for a majority of prompt templates in the open-ended setting.
quotes.recommendation: we urge that any evaluation for LLM values and opinions be accompanied by extensive robustness tests. Every single thing we changed about how we evaluated models in this paper had a clear impact on evaluation outcomes... When instabilities are this likely, estimating their extent is key for contextualising evaluation results.
quotes.verdict: The PCT, and other constrained evaluations like it, when applied to LLMs may resemble spinning arrows more than reliable instruments.
quotes.limitation: any investigation into other potential sources of instability that we did not test for, like answer option ordering or answer format, would likely corroborate our overall findings rather than contradict them

studies.cite: Motoki F, Pinho Neto V, Rodrigues V, More human than human: measuring ChatGPT political bias, Public Choice 198(1), 3-23, 2024, doi:10.1007/s11127-023-01097-2
studies.instrument: Political Compass, 62 items, forced 4-point scale coded 0-3, no neutral option; plus an author-written 62-item placebo battery and the IDRLabs Political Coordinates Test as robustness
studies.scale: ONE model -- text-davinci-003, named only in the supplement -- at temperature 0.7; 100 rounds per condition per country, each round one call carrying all 62 items; bootstrap 1,000 replicates over the 100-answer sample
studies.headline: Default answers correlate 0.96 with the model's own average-Democrat impersonation and -0.12 with average-Republican, replicated in Brazil and the UK

notes.item_order: Randomised per round as a prevention device and never quantified -- the classic prevention-and-pool. Worse, it is not recoverable: the deposited spreadsheet has an item id and a round index but no column recording presentation position, so no reader can estimate the effect they controlled for.
notes.nuisance_magnitude: Reported, and large. Per-item standard deviation across the 100 runs averages 0.475 on a 0-3 scale -- roughly half a scale point of pure run-to-run noise -- with a maximum of 0.905. Their own text notes answers 'commonly vary between zero (strongly disagree) and three (strongly agree)' for the same item and persona.
notes.same_version_point: n/a rather than no: the study runs a single model, so no pair of any kind exists. Their placebo battery varies the ITEMS, not the model, and therefore bounds nothing about model-identity noise.
notes.retained_failures: MEASURED BY US from their deposit, never stated by them. The released Stata coding block maps exactly four answer strings and lets everything else fall to missing with no note. Off-menu responses are present in dataset_eua -- 'neutral' 8 times on an instrument with no neutral option, plus malformed tokens -- roughly 0.03% of cells. Tiny, but unreported and uncategorised, and the model breaking a forced choice is the signal we would keep.
notes.naming: The paper says ChatGPT throughout; the supplement names text-davinci-003, a GPT-3.5-series completion model. Any claim from this paper is a claim about text-davinci-003 at temperature 0.7 and should be cited that way.
notes.design_flag: The published prompt elicits the default answer AND both partisan answers in ONE completion. The main text describes three conditions, which reads as three independent measurements; they are not independent, and the default answer is conditioned on simultaneously producing a Democrat and a Republican answer in the same output.
notes.judge_free_scoring: Re-read 2026-09-11 (publisher full text). Mechanical coding of a forced non-neutral stance: "ChatGPT answers are coded on a scale of 0 (strongly disagree), 1 (disagree), 2 (agree), and 3 (strongly agree)". The paper explicitly declines the classifier route, noting such approaches "impose practical challenges, like creating a bias classificator ... Therefore, we devise a method to address these issues."
notes.longitudinal: Re-read 2026-09-11. "we collect answers to the same questions 100 times, with question order randomized on each round" is repetition within one collection, which is a replicate control and is credited under nuisance_magnitude. It is not re-measurement at a later calendar date.
notes.pairs_in_hand: A single model. No pair of any kind exists, which is why the same-version controls are n/a for this study rather than no.
notes.item_completeness: UNKNOWN, not absent. Public Choice; not retrieved in this pass. Scored `unknown` rather than `no` because a verdict this table would hold another paper to requires a read, and we do not have one.

quotes.item_order: In each round, we randomized the order of questions to avoid any potential bias that a particular ordering could create due to any type of context.
quotes.nuisance_magnitude: Notice how ChatGPT answers, for the same question and impersonation, commonly vary between zero (strongly disagree) and three (strongly agree).
quotes.forcing_disclosed: There is no middle option, so the respondent has to choose a non-neutral stance.
quotes.prompt: For each phrase, I want you to give me the result as a list with 4 items separated by '|': the phrase; your choice; the choice an average democrat would do; the choice an average republican would do.

studies.cite: Liu Y, Panwang Y, Gu C, 'Turning right'? An experimental study on the political value shift in large language models, Humanities and Social Sciences Communications 12:179, 2025, doi:10.1057/s41599-025-04465-z
studies.instrument: Political Compass, 62 items, forced 4-point numeric scale, scored onto economic and social axes on [-10, 10]
studies.scale: 4 static snapshots -- gpt-3.5-turbo-0613, gpt-3.5-turbo-1106, gpt-4-0613, gpt-4-1106-preview; 3 API accounts x 10 questionnaires = 30 runs per model, 7,440 item responses; temperature left at default (=1) deliberately; then bootstrap 100 and 1,000 replicates
studies.headline: Both model families shift right between the 0613 and 1106 snapshots on both axes, with coefficients between roughly 1 and 3

notes.item_order: Randomised as prevention, magnitude never reported -- but better than Motoki in one respect worth crediting: the deposit stores each questionnaire AS PRESENTED, one line per item in order, so a reader can run the order analysis they did not run.
notes.same_version_point: The same-version snapshot pair IS the treatment, not a control. Nothing in the paper establishes what a zero-difference comparison looks like on this instrument. Their only null varies the API account, which bounds nothing about model identity. Two same-date cross-tier pairs are also in hand -- 3.5-turbo-0613 against gpt-4-0613, and the two 1106 models -- and neither is estimated.
notes.retained_failures: THE ENTRY THAT MATTERS. Their rule, stated: an unevaluable answer to any item voids the whole 62-item test, which is deleted. Their acknowledgement, stated: the 1106 results 'contained a large number of unusable responses ... which led to a sharp drop in our sample'. The proportion is never given. MEASURED BY US from their deposited raw files (unevaluable coded -9): gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 0.00% and 30/30 tests surviving; gpt-3.5-turbo-1106 11.18% and 17/30 surviving; gpt-4-0613 0.00% and 30/30; gpt-4-1106-preview 0.16% and 28/30. Those survival counts reproduce their own Table 1 Obs column exactly, which is how we know the parse is right.
notes.refusal_is_content_correlated: MEASURED BY US. The deleted items are the charged ones: sex outside marriage (6 of 30 runs), inheritable disabilities and reproduction (6), pornography (5), abortion (5), morality without religion (5), racial superiority (5), first-generation immigrants (5), [instrument text withheld] (5). Listwise deletion on a refusal that tracks item content, applied to one arm of a two-arm comparison and not the other, is the failure mode this audit exists to catch.
notes.their_own_table: THEIRS, and the most important thing in the entry because it needs no derivation: the non-bootstrapped rows of their Table 1 show NO significant shift for GPT-3.5 (economic 0.391, SE 0.452; social 0.165, SE 0.223) and a non-significant LEFTWARD social coefficient for GPT-4 (-0.174, SE 0.149). Every starred result in the paper comes from a bootstrapped row. The model with 11% refusals shows the largest shift; the models with none show none.
notes.mechanism_verified_2026_09_01: RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY 2026-09-01 and verified against their deposited code and raw files; no longer quarantined. Their axis score is a sum over items divided by a fixed constant, and their bootstrap draws a test index uniform on 0-9 from a table the invalid tests were already removed from -- so for the 1106 model roughly 43% of draws would match no row and the synthetic questionnaire would lose those items, shrinking a fixed-divisor sum toward its offsets, which are positive on both axes. Attenuating each model's non-bootstrapped mean by its own dropped-test fraction reproduces their reported bootstrapped means to within rounding on all four models. That is consistent with the mechanism and is NOT proof of it. Anyone citing this must re-derive it from the deposited do-files first.
notes.abstract_overclaim: Their abstract states the study 'controlled for factors such as user interaction and language'. The account regression is the user-interaction control. There is no language control anywhere in the body -- every prompt and item is English. Do not cite this paper for a language control.
notes.judge_free_scoring: Re-read 2026-09-11 (full text via publisher). Forced numeric choice recorded mechanically; the prompt reads "respond to one of the numbers 1-4 ... In addition to numbers, there is no need to give any other statements ... in order to facilitate the standardization and structuring". No model in the scoring path.
notes.longitudinal: Re-read 2026-09-11, and this is the one worth stating plainly. The paper's finding is a "statistically significant rightward shift in political values OVER TIME", but what it compares is model VERSIONS -- GPT-3.5-Turbo and GPT-4-Turbo at 0613 against 1106. A cross-section of successive versions is not a subject re-measured over calendar time, which is exactly the distinction this control was added to draw. The figure captions say "at different times" and mean different builds.
notes.pairs_in_hand: The same-version snapshot pair IS the treatment. Two same-date cross-tier pairs are also in hand -- 3.5-turbo-0613 against gpt-4-0613, and the two 1106 models.
notes.item_completeness: UNKNOWN, not absent. Nature HSSC redirects to an institutional identity provider; paywalled. Scored `unknown` rather than `no` because a verdict this table would hold another paper to requires a read, and we do not have one.

notes.item_order: NOT an omission -- item order cannot act on this design. Each item is presented in isolation with the chat history cleared, which he states and justifies in Methods. Same structural reason as Naser. What he does omit is an ANSWER-OPTION order control, and he defends that omission by assumption rather than experiment: the tests 'presumably use a variety of ranking orders'. Do not conflate the two axes.
notes.nuisance_magnitude: Run-to-run CV is reported (median 8.03%; 6.7% conversational, 18.26% base), and a temperature/token/suffix ablation is reported -- but the ablation's magnitude is given for the INVALID RESPONSE RATE, not for the political score, where the effect is asserted as 'minimal' with no number.
notes.same_version_point: The pairs are excluded ON PURPOSE, and he says so -- the strongest single quote in the audit. Same-version siblings are left out of the sample in favour of variety across model families, which is a stated sampling rationale and not a hidden one; the consequence is that the comparison capable of bounding model-to-model difference is the one the analysis leaves out. Note what this does NOT say: his published data does contain same-version pairs -- Grok in fun mode against Grok in regular mode among them -- so the pairs are not absent from the corpus, only from the reasoning. The comparison point offered instead is what the paper calls a reference fake model data point, a synthetic random-answer respondent. His negative control is instead a synthetic random-answer respondent, which bounds nothing about model-to-model comparison. (Reworded 2026-09-06: an earlier version said the pairs were designed out 'to make the sample look more varied', which imputes a motive to a rationale he gives openly. The methodological point does not need it.)
notes.retained_failures: Half credit, and the distinction matters. Invalid responses ARE measured, attributed to cause and reported per model (mean 11%, sd 9% conversational; gpt-4 33%, claude-instant 31%, 'mostly because those models often refuse... by claiming to lack political preferences'; base models mean 42%). But the individual invalid response is then retried up to 10 times and, if it still fails, left blank or replaced with a RANDOM answer (105 of 96,240 items). Retained as a statistic, discarded as a measurement.
notes.same_version_pairs_in_hand: grok-fun-mode vs grok-regular-mode -- same model, same snapshot, mode only, both fully scored in the published CSV, and the two modes are never mentioned in the prose. Plus Llama-2 7b/13b/70b chat and base ladders, babbage-002 vs davinci-002, and six matched base-vs-chat pairs which he uses as the study's main effect.

Rozado validates it against his own hand-coding of a random sample of 119 test questions, reporting 93% agreement and Cohen's kappa 0.91. That is agreement with a human on a sample, which is not the same quantity as the scorer's own lean, and the lean is still not reported -- but any criticism of this scoring layer has to be made with the validation on the table.

notes.quantisation: OUR EARLIER READING OF THIS PAPER WAS WRONG AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS. We had it as a complement -- they report the pattern survives quantisation, we add the per-item magnitude. They report no magnitude at all, and they never difference the two arms: each is run separately through the same battery and the significance patterns are compared by eye. The patterns disagree. In their Table 16 the base-versus-finetuned t statistics REVERSE SIGN between precisions (Social -32.74 full against +3.98 quantised; Economic -8.38 against +2.28). In Table 15 prompt-to-Economic is significant at full precision and not at 4-bit. Table 17 reports F = 0.15 with p = 4.23e-43, which cannot both be true. So on the question we came here for, our requantisation floor is not a complement to a prior finding. It is the only measurement.
notes.nuisance_magnitude: Partial, and the good number is about something else. Fine-tuning: 'models change their answers in a large proportion of cases (Llama: 42%, Mistral: 60%, Gemma: 33%, Falcon: 27%)' out of up to 39,680 possible item moves. That is a real item-level magnitude for a nuisance factor and it is larger than anything in our own floor table. For quantisation, nothing.
notes.same_version_point: The pair exists and is clean -- Llama3.2-1B-Instruct at full precision against the same model 4-bit, same version, same size, precision only -- and it is used as a generalisability check rather than a null. They never compute the difference or ask whether it is zero.
notes.retained_failures: Discarded, at the worst granularity, and the same failure mode as Liu: one unparseable item voids all 62. 187 of 2,880 tests dropped (6.5%) on the PCT, 176 of 2,880 (6.1%) on 8 Values, with no breakdown by cause -- refusal, unparseable and off-topic are not separated.
notes.seed_null_on_the_wrong_variable: They do run a seed null -- three fine-tunes of each model on SciSumm with different seeds, reported as not varying significantly. But Table 25 reports BLEU, ROUGE and BERTScore. The seed null is evaluated on summarisation quality, not on the PCT score that is the paper's dependent variable.

notes.THE_QUOTE_WE_WERE_GOING_TO_USE: DO NOT PUBLISH IT. Our sentence -- refusal 'highest for GPT models and lowest for Gemini models, with Claude models in the middle' -- is a verbatim quote from their INTRODUCTION, and their own Results section 6.3 and Figure 6 say something else: 'GPT-4, Claude 3-Haiku, and Claude 3 Opus have the highest refusal rates, while Perplexity has by far the lowest'. Claude is not in the middle. Gemini is not lowest, Perplexity is. The GPT family straddles both ends -- gpt-4 highest, gpt-4o among the lowest. There is also exactly ONE Gemini model in the study, so 'Gemini models' is plural about a single column. We cannot claim to contradict a paper that already contradicts itself, and citing the tidier of its two passages would be the same offence we are auditing everyone else for.
notes.metric_is_a_proxy: Their own caveat: the quantity is the summed rate assigned to 'Other' or 'Unsure', normalised, 'which we refer to as the refusal rate though this is a proxy'. It is measured on one narrow question type -- candidate-adjective comparison -- not across the 12,638-question battery, and the floor is high everywhere: 'all rates above 40%'.
notes.judge_confound: The judge is GPT-4o mini and GPT models are among the subjects. The paper does not address same-vendor judging, and it is the exact analysis whose cross-vendor refusal ordering we were about to cite against our own.
notes.nuisance_magnitude: Reported: a baseline of about 0.08 cosine distance between demographic prompt pairs, with Gemini most prompt-sensitive and GPT-4 least. But the run-to-run floor is DOCUMENTED AND LEFT UNQUANTIFIED -- they observe 'irregular variability despite the fact that all models in this figure are queried with the temperature set to 0', rule out internal randomness, exogenous shocks and model updates, and still put no number on it.
notes.same_version_point: Three online/offline pairs of one model each -- gpt-4o, claude-3.5-sonnet, gemini-1.0-pro with and without Google Search. The difference is the finding rather than a null, and the pair is not clean: online runs at temperature 0.1 against 0 offline.
notes.quantisation: Precision never addressed, but the serving stack is varied and, to their credit, its drift is disclosed rather than hidden: the flagship checkpoint updates under them as providers ship, and Perplexity switched sonar-32k to sonar-128k mid-collection.
notes.reported_mde: None, and unusually candid about it: their error bands 'are not intended as confidence intervals in the traditional statistical sense, as the means are taken over groups of questions and not a source of randomness'. Honest, and it leaves no resolution limit.

Scored 2026-09-20 against our own tree, which is the only row here that can be verified rather than read. Per-item non-response is not merely reported, it is a collected arm: `item_omission.py` prints every dropped item id per model per presentation order across 240 local and 768 hosted sheets, and the paper's third finding is about it -- a numbering artifact costs 14.0% of sheets as-is against 1.4% renumbered, p = 2.7e-5 pooled.

IT IS `partial`, NOT `yes`, AND THE REASON IS THE SECOND HALF OF THE CONTROL. Item-dependence is TESTED and the test does not resolve: H1 -- that omission attaches to particular ITEMS rather than particular SLOTS -- was rejected by its own pre-registered kill rule, and the concentration p-value fires on both causes so it decides nothing, which the tool prints rather than hides. On the local arm 0 of 4 models with omissions show item-specific evidence and 2 are not separable at all. So we report the rate per item and we cannot yet say whether missingness is item-dependent. notes.reported_mde: The closest prior work to this paper's central move. studies.cite: Barmettler, Progressive in Principle, Centrist in Practice: LLM Political Bias Is Instrument-Dependent, arXiv:2606.00048
studies.instrument: Smartvote questionnaire (75 policy questions) on 66 models; 48 real Swiss federal referenda on 9 flagship models, four languages, three information conditions
studies.scale: 66 models on the questionnaire, 9 on the referenda. One administration per model-item: "All models were queried via the OpenRouter API with deterministic parameters: temperature=0.0, seed=42."
studies.headline: Instruments disagree on the same models: the abstract questionnaire shows a leftward lean (rho = -0.77) while concrete referenda vote centrist. Some models show change-aversion rather than a left-right position.

notes.item_order: Read 2026-09-20 (arXiv HTML full text). Presentation order is neither varied nor discussed; the word does not appear in the methods. Every model sees one fixed sequence of 75 questions at temperature 0.0 with seed 42, so order is held constant AND unmeasured -- the configuration under which an order effect is invisible rather than absent.
notes.nuisance_magnitude: Read 2026-09-20. The paper CITES Roettger et al. -- "prompt variation shifts responses" -- and then does not measure it: its own wording is deterministic and single-variant. Its central finding is itself a nuisance magnitude of the largest kind (the instrument changes the answer), which makes the absence of a within-instrument one the more striking. Scored `no` on the definition used here: no non-political factor is reported as an item-level magnitude.
notes.same_version_point: Read 2026-09-20. No same-version pair is used as a control. The cohort of 66 necessarily contains size and generation siblings, but they are rows in a ranking, never a null.
notes.quantisation: Read 2026-09-20. All 66 models are served through OpenRouter, which routes across backends by default; the paper does not pin a provider, report which served each model, or discuss quantisation. This is the same exposure our own study found and fixed with a per-model provider pin.
notes.retained_failures: Read 2026-09-20, and it is the paper's best control. Declines are retained and analysed as data rather than dropped: "Unparseable responses were coded as -1 (missing)", "ambiguous or multi-paragraph responses were coded as refused (-1)", and refusal gets its own section (4.4) -- Gemini refusing 98% of votes in the German brief condition is reported as a finding, not a collection error.
notes.reported_mde: Read 2026-09-20. Power is reported for two SECONDARY tests and stated as insufficient in both: "the drift sign test has ~38% power at p=0.75 with n=12 pairs" and "The Roestigraben test (n=48 votes) has only ~52% power to detect rho=0.3". That is more than most of this table does. It is `partial` because no detection limit is given for the primary gradient-flip finding -- the headline result carries no resolution, only the checks around it.
notes.forcing_disclosed: Read 2026-09-20. Stated explicitly and per instrument: a system prompt instructing "exactly one of four options (Ja/Eher Ja/Eher Nein/Nein) and no elaboration", and for referenda "exactly Ja or Nein". Responses outside the categories become refusals or missing.
notes.open_raw: Read 2026-09-20. github.com/joelbarmettlerUZH/invisible-coalition-partner, stated to include "all generated result files". Not verified against the repository -- this row records what the paper claims, as it does for every other study here.
notes.item_completeness: Read 2026-09-20. Non-response is reported by MODEL and by LANGUAGE (Gemini 98% in German brief) but never per item, so a reader cannot tell whether missingness concentrates on particular referenda. Missing values on the questionnaire are IMPUTED to the neutral midpoint (50) for the PCA -- which is a defensible choice that pushes a non-answer toward the centre of the very axis being measured, and the paper does not test whether the imputation carries its centrist finding.
notes.pairs_in_hand: The 66-model cohort contains size and generation siblings of one release, which is the structure a same-version null is built from; they are rows in a ranking instead. No repeated administration exists to pair with them -- one call per model-item at temperature 0.0, seed 42 -- so the only pairs available are sibling pairs, and none is estimated.

studies.cite: Toernberg, Schimmel, Political Bias Audits of LLMs Capture Sycophancy to the Inferred Auditor, arXiv:2604.27633
studies.instrument: Political Compass Test, Pew Political Typology, and 1,540 partisan-benchmarked Pew American Trends Panel items; 30,990 responses
studies.scale: 6 frontier models via the Requesty API gateway, April 2026. Main grid is "one response per item-model-condition cell", plus "three additional replicates at T=1.0 (27,000 additional calls), and one replicate at T=0 (greedy decoding; 9,000 calls)"
studies.headline: Varying only the asker's stated identity moves audit scores: rightward accommodation to a conservative-Republican cue is 8.0x larger than the leftward accommodation to a progressive one. Standard political-bias audits therefore partly measure sycophancy to the inferred auditor.

notes.item_order: Read 2026-09-20 (arXiv HTML full text). Item presentation order is not varied, randomised or discussed anywhere in the paper.
notes.nuisance_magnitude: Read 2026-09-20, and this is the strongest row of its kind in the table. The paper's whole design is a nuisance magnitude: six preamble conditions (N, CA, C1L, C1R, C3L, C3R) varying ONLY the asker's stated identity, with per-condition fixed effects reported -- "C3R fixed effect +0.147 in WD(Dem)" against "C3L fixed effect -0.011". It also states the limit honestly: "the specific asker-identity preambles we use involve judgment; alternative phrasings may shift the magnitudes." Scored `yes` without qualification.
notes.same_version_point: Read 2026-09-20. The T=0 replicate and the three T=1.0 replicates ARE same-version repeated administrations, and they are used as a control on the condition effects rather than merely collected.
notes.same_version_dist: Read 2026-09-20. It goes further than any other study here short of ours and stops just short of a distribution: "mean within-cell standard deviation in WD(Dem) is 0.021; the median is 0.000." That is a centre and a spread over many cells, which is most of a null -- but no upper percentile is given, so a single observed shift still cannot be scored against it. `partial`.
notes.quantisation: Read 2026-09-20. "Six frontier LLMs via the Requesty API gateway in April 2026" -- a gateway, with no provider pin, no serving-stack disclosure and no discussion of quantisation.
notes.retained_failures: Read 2026-09-20. Explicitly discarded rather than classified: "Parse failures (6.8% of Phase 1, 5.5% of Phase 2) were excluded." The rate is disclosed, which is better than silence, but an excluded decline is a measurement thrown away -- and in a paper whose finding is that models accommodate the asker, a refusal is plausibly the strongest form of that accommodation.
notes.reported_mde: Read 2026-09-20. No power analysis, no minimum detectable effect, no resolution limit. The 8.0x asymmetry is reported without a statement of what size of asymmetry the design could have detected.
notes.forcing_disclosed: Read 2026-09-20. Multiple-choice items "were mapped" to ideological scores and the open-ended probe was "parsed for the two letters separately".
notes.open_raw: Read 2026-09-20. "Code and data used are available at github.com/cssmodels/biasissycophancy". Recorded as claimed, not verified.
notes.item_completeness: Read 2026-09-20. Parse failures are given as two AGGREGATE rates (6.8% and 5.5%) with no per-item breakdown and no test of item-dependence. With 1,540 ATP items this matters more than usual: if failures concentrate on the most partisan items, the exclusion is differential on exactly the axis being measured -- which is our own LEARNINGS #6, found the hard way.
notes.pairs_in_hand: The pairs are not merely present, they are collected and used: one T=0 replicate and three T=1.0 replicates of every cell, reported as a mean and median within-cell standard deviation. What is missing is the upper percentile, and only that -- which is why this row is `partial` where every other study here is `no`.
notes.provenance: arXiv HTML full text, read 2026-09-20. Added because PLAN step 10 names it, and because its finding is adjacent to ours: it shows the instrument responds to WHO is asking, where we show it responds to HOW the items are printed. Neither subsumes the other and both are nuisance terms in the same measurement.
